ai.summary: The v9 series adds Counter delegation (Smcdeleg/Ssccfg) support, which depends on the Smcsrind/Sscsrind indirect CSR extensions and lets S-mode program hpmevent and hpmcounters directly without SBI calls [1]. Sashiko AI review raised a number of issues across the series: the Ssccfg and Smcdeleg validation checks were reported as depending on the wrong extension variants [2], the indirect CSR macros were flagged for local variable names that could shadow caller arguments [3], and several problems were found in the counter discovery and SBI PMU probe code, including disabled firmware counters, 32-bit bitmask collisions, a stubbed delegation discovery path, and resource cleanup on probe failure [4, 5]. Further findings concerned the counter-delegation enable path, the legacy event sysfs macro, QEMU vendor event masks, and config2 mapping for legacy and raw events [6, 7, 8, 9]. Version 9 addressed some of these, including the probe-time panic on fixed counters, the sbi_v3_available placement, and rejecting config2 values above bit 31, and it dropped the test-only patches [1]. Paul Walmsley queued the first ten patches into riscv/for-next and deferred the rest to a later period, which Atish Patra accepted [10, 11]. Anup Patel then gave Reviewed-by tags to patches 4, 10, 11, 12 and 15 without further comment [12, 13, 14, 15, 16].

ai.summary: The series, posted by Clément Léger as v3 and v4 in November 2023, extends the riscv hwprobe syscall so userspace can discover many more ISA extensions, including Zfh[min], Zvfh[min], Zihintntl, Zbc, the vector and scalar crypto families, and Zfa [1, 13]. Several extensions are shorthands for sub-extensions, and a bundled-extension mechanism was added so that only the sub-extensions are exposed through hwprobe [1, 13]. Reviewers asked for a comment explaining why the bundled-extension handling is safe [5], and Evan Green suggested using a pointer rather than copying a struct into a local [6]. Jerry Shih pointed out that Zvknha and Zvknhb are exclusive rather than in a superset relationship [7], and after a mail-client mix-up [8, 9] and a follow-up in which Shih cited OpenSSL checking either extension [10], Léger agreed to stop treating Zvknhb as a superset [11, 13]. Conor Dooley noted that the dt-bindings text should not mention hwprobe [3], which Léger accepted and removed in v4 [12, 13]. Dooley also asked that the Zkr seed-CSR binding state that the CSR is accessible at the privilege level the devicetree is provided for [2], and v4 added that wording [13]. Dooley later flagged a mismatch between the v4 cover letter's "only" wording and the binding text [15].

commit.subject: RISC-V: Probe Svinval extension form ISA string

ai.summary: The Svinval series adds support for the Svinval extension, first as a Linux kernel TLB-flush change by Mayuresh Chitale and later as a KVM RISC-V change by Anup Patel, with the feature probed from the ISA string [1, 6]. Reviewers asked that Svinval be probed in riscv_fill_hwcap() [2], and Palmer Dabbelt noted unresolved IRQ feedback from Marc on the RFC v2 cover letter [4]. Palmer also questioned whether splitting sfence.vma into sinval.vma sequences would help performance unless other work could overlap the flushes, and suggested that the TLB model would need splitting into phases to benefit [9]. Mayuresh replied that the approach matches the non-normative text in the privileged spec and that the extension is off by default and enabled only through the device tree, with no expected change to the software TLB model [10]. Alexandre Ghiti asked whether any benchmarks had been run, and Mayuresh answered that only stress-ng and kernel selftests had been used [11, 12]. Across versions, the kernel series went from RFC v1 with a new tlb.S assembly file [1] to RFC v2, rebased on 5.18-rc3 with the hwcap probe added [3], and then to RFC v3, which fixed the vma passed to the sinval instructions, unified the static-key mechanism for Svinval, and rebased on torvalds/master [5]. The KVM series in v1 was reviewed by Andrew Jones [7] and queued for 6.1 by Anup Patel [8].

commit.subject: riscv: Add support for non-coherent devices using zicbom extension

1631ba1259d6.title: riscv: implement Zicbom-based CMO instructions + the t-head variant

earlier.title: riscv: Implement Zicbom-based cache management operations

ai.summary: The series adds Zicbom-based cache-management (CMO) operations to the RISC-V kernel, plus a T-Head variant that drives the Allwinner D1's different cache instructions through the alternatives mechanism, mainly so non-coherent DMA devices work [1, 26, 58]. Early reviewers asked whether the cache block size should be a runtime value rather than L1_CACHE_BYTES, and Anup Patel argued that a firmware- or DT-supplied size avoids incomplete range operations on cores with smaller blocks [2, 4]. Philipp Tomsich's question about a fixed block size was answered by the same point that compliant platforms will converge on one size while the kernel should still work with others [3, 4]. The T-Head errata raised an objection that the cache instructions had to be in the assembler, and Heiko Stuebner asked whether to wait for binutils or use encoded instructions for the D1 [5, 6]. Samuel Holland's D1 testing showed MMC, USB and Ethernet broken without the option, and a DMA buffer-corruption report from Corentin Labbe was explained by the cache semantics of DMA_FROM_DEVICE, not a fault in the series [9, 10, 11, 13]. Christoph Hellwig asked for the device-coherency model to default to coherent with explicit non-coherent marking, which led to the of_dma_is_coherent() change and a new dma-noncoherent DT property accepted by the maintainers [33, 36, 39, 42, 45, 51]. Holland also found that the flush and invalidate operations were on the wrong paths and that the T-Head version broke Ethernet because buffers were not cache-block aligned, and these were corrected in later versions [30, 31, 48]. Guo Ren's review was carried forward and a wrong RV32 ABI check in Kconfig was fixed in v7 [50, 57, 60]. Palmer Dabbelt accepted the series for next, noting it had to be merged with pre-encoded T-Head instructions and with Zicbom made to depend on MMU [61, 63].

commit.subject: riscv: add ISA extension parsing for Zcmop

164d644059cf.title: Add support for a few Zc* extensions as well as Zcmop

ai.summary: The series adds ISA string parsing, hwprobe export and KVM support for Zimop, Zcmop, Zca, Zcf, Zcd and Zcb, and reviewers initially questioned whether Zc* subsets should be inferred from C/F/D, with Conor Dooley objecting to devicetree churn and asking that dependencies be handled in the kernel rather than the binding [22, 26, 30]. Clément Léger proposed resolving ISA extensions in two phases with per-extension validate() callbacks that can return -EPROBE_DEFER, which Conor Dooley accepted after discussing the approach and the remaining looping concern [35, 37, 39, 40, 50, 53]. Dependency rules were moved out of the devicetree and into the kernel, and Zcf's validate() checks for F and a 32-bit kernel [22, 32, 40, 53, 57, 58]. Anup Patel acked the KVM changes in v2 and v5 [16, 17, 18, 19, 55, 56], and Charlie Jenkins noted conflicts with his xandespmu removal and KVM SSCOFPMF changes that were resolved by rebasing [61, 65, 66], while Zimop was merged into the series in v5 to avoid cross-series dependencies [54, 67, 68]. Across versions the series went from v1 with dt-bindings dependency checks, through v2 and v3 with the ISA-string validation rework, to v4 with validate() callbacks, to v5 which folded in Zimop and reworked the resolution loop, and v6 and v7 which were rebased onto riscv/for-next, with the final changes being cosmetic rewrites of conditionals and renames [54, 74, 75, 76, 78, 79] [15, 34, 38].

commit.subject: riscv: Implement cmpxchg8/16() using Zabha

ai.summary: The series adds Zacas and Zabha based cmpxchg and xchg implementations, plus qspinlock support on RISC-V, with the later versions also adding Ziccrse [71, 100, 131, 146]. Reviewers initially objected to enabling experimental extensions by default, and the resolution was to avoid that and to require toolchains that support the ratified extensions, with LLVM 17+ adopted as the minimum for the cmpxchg32/64 changes [2, 3, 12, 52, 68, 69]. Andrea Parri raised ordering concerns about the fully-ordered LR/SC and AMO mappings, which were addressed by using aqrl semantics and restricting the optimisation to fully-ordered operations [4, 5, 40, 42, 43, 49, 57]. The main qspinlock concern was that the extensions are only discovered after spinlocks are first used, which led to starting with qspinlocks and switching to ticket spinlocks through a static key, with combo spinlocks added as a Kconfig option [16, 18, 22, 29, 53, 64, 66, 67, 68, 126]. Forward-progress requirements were debated, with Guo Ren proposing Ziccrse as the guarantee and the series adopting it [24, 54, 71]. Reviewers asked for fixes to the Zawrs build failure, header cleanups, clearer Kconfig help text recommending combo spinlocks, and a measured kernel size impact, which Alexandre reported as small in the ELF and .text sections [106, 107, 117, 128, 142]. The v6 posting still carried a static-key approach that Will Deacon flagged as fragile, and after merge it was reported to break boot with combo spinlocks enabled, with Guo Ren identifying a deadlock with RT mutexes during jump-label patching and proposing fixes [150, 152, 153, 158, 165, 166].

ai.summary: The series adds Linux kernel support for the Zicond, Zacas and Ztso ISA extensions, exporting them through the hwprobe interface for userspace, with the aim of covering extensions present in RVA22U64/RVA23U64 [1, 6]. ai.summary: The series adds runtime detection of the Svnapot extension, letting the kernel use NAPOT-contiguous PTEs for hugetlb pages and huge vmap, gated by a Kconfig option that defaults to on [1, 12]. Reviewers asked for the Kconfig symbol to follow the RISCV_ISA_ naming and for its text to explain the memory cost of enabling it on systems with HUGETLBFS [4, 11, 60, 79]. They also raised the use of the alternatives framework versus static keys, with the author moving to static keys in v6 and later back to alternatives in v9 for heavily used inline functions [14, 22, 33, 49, 51]. Other review points covered hugetlb code duplicating arm64 and generic logic, a request to split out the best_map_size change from the linear-mapping patch, and a request for a pte_napot_shift handling with napot_cont_order and napot_pte_num helpers [17, 27, 34, 46, 61, 25]. Reviewers pointed to build breakage on rv32 and in allmodconfig, which was fixed in later revisions [41, 45, 8, 9]. The series was reduced over time: linear-mapping code was dropped into a separate patch in v7, leaving three patches covering pte format, hugetlb, and huge vmap, and v12 was rebased onto the new ISA extension API while v13 fixed patchwork-reported warnings [30, 76, 85, 93]. The remaining rough edges were the HUGE_MAX_HSTATE sizing and a Kconfig text warning, which the author kept as the simplest wording [67, 68, 75, 80, 82].

commit.subject: riscv: add ISA extension parsing for Zimop

2467c2104f1f.title: Add support for a few Zc* extensions, Zcmop and Zimop

earlier.title: Add parsing for Zimop ISA extension

ai.summary: The series adds support for Zimop, Zcmop, Zca, Zcf, Zcd and Zcb across ISA string parsing, hwprobe and KVM, and it changes ISA string handling to a two-phase parse-then-validate approach because C implies Zca, Zcf (on RV32 with F) and Zcd (with D) [1, 21]. Reviewers asked for the validation callback logic in the Zca/Zcf/Zcd/Zcb code to be written out as plain conditionals with early returns rather than compact ternary-style expressions [6], and Clément Léger agreed, proposing an IS_ENABLED() form for the Zcf check [7]. Charlie Jenkins noted that Zimop's ISA key number clashed with the pending XANDESPMU removal and suggested keeping the XANDESPMU entry and assigning Zimop key 75, leaving resolution to the maintainer [8]. Conflicts with recently merged patches on the KVM side and the ISA parsing side were raised as well, with Charlie noting that a dependency on his xtheadvector changes had not been stated in the cover letter, and Clément clarifying that the series was based on riscv/for-next, which already contained some of those patches [12, 13, 14, 15, 16]. Across versions, v6 removed the ternary operators in favour of if() checks as requested [21], and v7 was rebased on riscv/for-next to resolve conflicts, with Conor Dooley's remaining nit about naming the validation callback "depends" rather than "validate" left as a minor point [22, 23, 24, 25].

commit.subject: riscv: Add ISA extension parsing for Ziccrse

2d36fe89d872.title: riscv: Add ISA extension parsing for Ziccrse

earlier.title: dt-bindings: riscv: Add Ziccrse ISA extension description

ai.summary: The v3 to v6 series (Alexandre Ghiti, with Guo Ren's ticket/queued spinlock work) adds Zacas and Zabha based cmpxchg/xchg implementations and qspinlock support for RISC-V, with Ziccrse used to justify the qspinlock forward-progress guarantee [1, 4, 12]. Reviewers asked for the ISA-extension dt-binding entries to go to the devicetree list, which was done in later versions [2, 3, 53]. Several technical points were raised and settled during review: the Zacas cas operand ordering was explained and made explicit [7, 8, 29, 34, 35]; the llvm-16 inline-asm and C23 label issues were worked around with a static-key-based check [9, 10, 11, 18, 22]; the choice of ISA extension pairing and big-endian support were discussed and left out of scope [14, 15, 16, 17]; and Andrea's compile warnings for combo configs were fixed [12, 19]. For qspinlock, Guo asked for a kernel-parameter switch and reviewers asked for Kconfig help text steering users towards COMBO spinlocks, with the Kconfig and jump-label changes adjusted in v4 and v5 [4, 38, 46, 47, 48]. Kernel size impact was measured and found to be small, with the jump table growing 8 to 62 percent depending on config but the .text section growing well under one percent [58, 72]. Version 6 was rebased and carried the reviewer tags forward [76, 77]. After v6 was merged, a boot failure on a RISC-V configuration with combo spinlocks was traced by Guo Ren to a static-key-driven switch of spinlock implementations during early boot, where jump-label patching took a mutex whose rt_mutex path used the lock being switched; the author stated the static key use is temporary pending early ISA extension parsing [84, 85, 90, 95, 96].

commit.subject: riscv: Add ISA extension parsing for pointer masking

2e6f6ea452aa.title: riscv: Add ISA extension parsing for pointer masking

earlier.title: RISC-V: KVM: Allow Smnpm and Ssnpm extensions for guests
KVM: riscv: selftests: Add Smnpm and Ssnpm to get-reg-list test

ai.summary: The series adds userspace pointer masking and a tagged address ABI for RISC-V, letting userspace configure Smnpm or Ssnpm (depending on the kernel's mode) through an extended PR_SET_TAGGED_ADDR_CTRL, with the kernel untagging user pointers in software since its own accesses use its own masking configuration [1, 19, 29, 36, 58]. Early review centred on whether per-CPU versus per-thread envcfg handling was needed: Samuel Holland argued that writing envcfg on every trap return was costly and proposed writing it at task switch, exec and relevant prctl calls, while Deepak Gupta preferred a single write point on trap return, and Andrew Jones and Deepak Gupta debated whether heterogeneous Zicboz support was worth the complexity [2, 3, 4, 8, 9, 11, 12, 13, 14, 15, 16, 17, 18]. Holland settled the approach by making the envcfg update go through a helper that writes the CSR only when the task is current, and by ptrace_check_attach ensuring tracees are descheduled during ptrace operations [10]. Across versions the series dropped the envcfg-split and is_compat_thread patches (moved to a separate series), updated the pointer masking spec references, renamed the selftest directory and CONFIG symbol, reworked PMLEN handling with an enum and per-mm context, added hwprobe and KVM guest exports, and in v5 moved to ratified spec text and expanded the ABI documentation [19, 20, 22, 23, 24, 25, 26, 27, 28, 29, 31, 32, 33, 35, 36, 46, 50, 53, 55, 58]. For KVM, Anup Patel and Holland agreed that Smnpm should be excluded from ONE_REG disabling for now, with later SBI FWFT work to revisit this, and v5 adopted that compromise [37, 38, 39, 40, 41, 42, 43, 44, 45, 54, 60].

ai.summary: The series, posted by Clément Léger as v1 on 2024-06-19, adds kernel support for the Zaamo and Zalrsc extensions, which the A extension is now described as being built from [1]. Its five patches cover a devicetree binding description, parsing of the two extensions in the kernel, export through hwprobe, KVM guest/VM permission, and a KVM selftest update [1]. Conor Dooley acked the devicetree binding and the parsing patch, with his comment on fragmentation in the extension list appearing only as a remark on the parsing patch [2, 3]. Charlie Jenkins reviewed the hwprobe export patch, and Anup Patel reviewed the KVM patches and their selftest update, all in December 2024 [4, 5, 6]. Anup later noted in the cover letter thread that the KVM patches conflicted with KVM work he had queued for Linux 6.14 and asked for an ACK so he could take them through the KVM RISC-V tree [7]. commit.subject: riscv: Add task switch support for vector

earlier.title: riscv: Add task switch support for vector

ai.summary: The series "riscv: Add vector ISA support" adds Linux support for the RISC-V V extension (based on the 1.0 spec) through many revisions, from v1 in January 2020 to v21 in June 2023 [1, 3, 17, 81, 102, 145, 198, 299]. The early versions targeted draft spec 0.8 and 0.9 and used a fixed 128-bit vlen, with reviewers asking for a dynamic-vlen ABI for sigcontext and ptrace [5, 17, 24, 25]. Reviewers pushed back on always-on vector state, questioning allocation cost and a process-wide default instead of explicit opt-in, which the later versions addressed [53, 61, 69, 73, 82, 83]. Greentime Hu drove the early versions while Andy Chiu took over from v13, and the design settled into allocating vector state on a first-use trap, with signal and ptrace state stored behind a new __riscv_v_ext_state structure [102, 145, 198, 226]. The first-use trap design and the ABI-compatibility concerns led to a prctl and sysctl interface, and ELF_HWCAP was changed to a function so the V bit reflects per-process availability [277, 278, 291, 299]. Final review concerns about the hwprobe semantics and the .option arch assembler check remained open after the series was applied [312, 319, 320] [306].

ai.summary: The Zicclsm series adds Zicclsm, along with Ziccamoa, Ziccif, Ziccrse, Za64rs, B, and Zic64b, to the RISC-V cpufeature parser and hwprobe interface, and in later revisions adds RVA23U64 base detection and reporting through /proc/cpuinfo and hwprobe [1, 85, 120, 151]. Reviewers asked that the vector unaligned-access probing mirror the scalar probing, that the probing run on all CPUs back to back, that CPU hotplug be handled, and that Zicclsm be dropped from the speed decision because the profile text does not say misaligned accesses are fast [2, 4, 5, 8, 16, 47, 49, 61, 70]. The "unknown" versus "slow" reporting for vector misaligned access was debated at length, and the state was eventually settled as UNKNOWN internally with explicit UNSUPPORTED, SLOW and FAST values [28, 72, 74, 78, 79, 80]. Reviewers pushed back on a Kconfig option to disable vector unaligned access, and the kernel-level consequences for vector crypto code were discussed without being settled in the series [29, 33, 34, 35, 38]. Across versions the series moved from Zicclsm-based speed assignment to probing-only detection, with the Zicclsm speed patches dropped in v4 and the RVA23U64 base added in later rounds [59, 61, 66, 109, 120, 139, 151]. The RVA23U64 series was reworked over v2 through v5 with changes to Zic64b validation, cbom/cbop/cboz block-size requirements in the dt-binding, and the B bundle handling, and several reviewers' Acked-by and Reviewed-by tags were collected along the way [108, 117, 120, 139, 151, 166, 169].

The remaining patches received Reviewed-by tags in v2 [9, 10, 11, 12]. Anup Patel's review of the KVM patches asked that the new KVM enum values be placed at the end of the enum for UAPI compatibility and that entries in kvm_isa_ext_arr[] and the selftest config table be kept in alphabetical order, and he stated these were handled at merge time [17, 18]. commit.subject: RISC-V: Enable sstc extension parsing from DT

ai.summary: The Sstc series adds supervisor-level timer compare registers (stimecmp and vstimecmp), letting the kernel program timer interrupts without an SBI call to M-mode, which is slow and, under KVM, emulated with a software timer [1, 2, 6, 19, 22, 23]. Its main reviewer concern was Jessica Clarke's objection that KVM writing vstimecmp inside the SBI set-timer handler clobbers S-mode state the ratified SBI spec does not permit, which he argued should block the patch until the spec was fixed [3, 7]. Atish Patra answered that a hypervisor cannot assume guests avoid Sstc or that a fixed-hrtimer path can cover it, since hardware compares vstimecmp every cycle once henvcfg.STCE is set and a stale value would cause spurious interrupts, so the SBI path must update vstimecmp directly [4, 8]. Anup Patel's review comments drove the code changes: he asked that the KVM timer reuse next_cycles, that the reset path set it to -1ULL to avoid an immediate interrupt for older guests, that pr_fmt and u64 conventions be applied, and that the new ISA extension enum be placed at the end of the UAPI array for compatibility [11, 12, 20]. He also asked for the KVM patches to be split out with Fixes tags and for the KVM mailing list to be copied, which Patra fixed [5, 16, 18]. Across versions the series went from an RFC with separate static-key and vstimer paths, replaced by function pointers and a single unified timer in v2, then trimmed of unrelated KVM fixes in v3, reworked around vcpu_load in v4 and v5, and had the enum moved and a compile error fixed in v6 and v7 [2, 6, 13, 19, 22, 23]. Palmer Dabbelt merged the non-KVM patches into riscv/for-next, and the KVM patch was merged there with Anup Patel's Acked-by once the dependent KVM changes were already upstream [28, 29, 30].

commit.subject: riscv: add RISC-V Svrsw60t59b extension support

59f6acb4be02.title: riscv: Add RISC-V Svrsw60t59b extension support

earlier.title: dt-bindings: riscv: Add Svrsw60t59b extension description

ai.summary: The series adds Svrsw60t59b extension support and soft-dirty and userfaultfd write-protect tracking for RISC-V, using PTE bits 59 and 60 [1, 3, 4, 6, 14]. Early reviewers asked for the new PTE checks to be runtime rather than compile-time, since Svrsw60t59b is a hardware extension, and Chunyan Zhang agreed that the checks must be run-time [6, 8]. Palmer Dabbelt raised concerns about unconditionally enabling VM_SOFTDIRTY on hardware lacking the extension and about the broken spec link, and asked for an architecture-level callback [11, 12], which led to the pgtable_supports_soft_dirty()/pgtable_supports_uffd_wp() macros that default to the CONFIG options and can be overridden per architecture [14, 15, 16, 17, 20, 22]. David Hildenbrand asked that VM_SOFTDIRTY never be set when soft-dirty is unsupported and that the CONFIG_MEM_SOFT_DIRTY and CONFIG_HAVE_ARCH_USERFAULTFD_WP ifdefs be removed in favour of these checks, and the series was reshaped accordingly by v12 [23, 24, 25, 26, 28, 31, 32]. Andrew Jones requested a reordering of the extension table entry and Conor Dooley requested a devicetree binding update, which was added in v13 [18, 33, 36, 40]. Build problems on 32-bit and no-MMU configurations and indentation issues were raised and fixed in later versions [34, 38, 39]. Across versions the series moved from a fixed-bit approach (v7) to dynamic availability macros (v9 onward), was renamed several times, and was rebased onto mm-new, and the final v15 was accepted into mm-unstable after a VMA test breakage was reported and a fix-up was proposed [44, 46, 47].

commit.subject: riscv: Detect the Ssqosid extension

5a17eb5f1c4c.title: riscv: add Ssqosid and CBQRI resctrl support

earlier.title: RISC-V: Detect Ssqosid extension and handle sqoscfg CSR
RISC-V: Add support for srmcfg CSR from Ssqosid ext
dt-bindings: riscv: Add Ssqosid extension description
RISC-V: QoS: enable resctrl support for Ssqosid

ai.summary: The series adds Ssqosid support (the srmcfg CSR and its context-switch handling) and an initial CBQRI resctrl integration limited to cache capacity allocation, with a DT-based platform driver, after earlier RFCs covering monitoring, bandwidth control and ACPI RQSC were narrowed down [1, 66, 72, 90, 104, 116, 121]. Reviewers, largely through Sashiko automated reviews, raised issues around CSR cache invalidation during CPU hotplug and suspend/resume, RV32 and 64-bit MMIO register access, missing checks on RCID and MCID counts, controller registration ordering, and locking between CPU hotplug and resctrl domain lists [2, 3, 7, 24, 26, 46, 47, 59, 73, 93, 95, 105, 106, 122, 124]. Drew Fustini generally settled these by explaining why certain concerns did not apply, such as the startup callback re-arming the cache sentinel and CPU hotplug locking ordering, and by changing the code where a concern was valid, for example adding a PM notifier, serializing the controller list, switching to 32-bit register accesses, and resolving domain membership from cache IDs [12, 33, 56, 60, 64, 65, 77, 81, 86, 88, 98, 107, 108, 114, 125, 126, 127]. Maintainer and reviewer comments on the devicetree binding led to a device-specific compatible requirement and a renamed node and compatible, and the Kconfig options were reworked so RISCV_CBQRI is user-selectable [75, 76, 78, 80, 96, 102]. Across versions the series moved from the broad RFC to a narrower allocation-only v1 and then iterated through v6 with these fixes [66, 72, 90, 104, 116, 121]. Paul Walmsley queued the first three patches for v7.3, with the srmcfg READ_ONCE() retained after Drew explained its purpose [128, 129, 131, 133]. A late report of an empty default cbm_mask was traced to a backport onto an older resctrl core and was not a problem in the v6 series itself [134, 135, 136] [1, 66, 72, 90, 104, 116, 121].

commit.subject: RISC-V: Detect Zicond from ISA string

662a601aa355.title: RISC-V: Detect Zicond from ISA string

earlier.title: RISC-V: KVM: Allow Zicond extension for Guest/VM
dt-bindings: riscv: Add Zicond extension entry

ai.summary: The series adds detection of the Zicond extension from the ISA string and lets KVM RISC-V guests discover and use it, with selftest coverage for the relevant registers [1, 15, 33]. Reviewers asked that the devicetree binding changes be split out from the kernel code, and Anup Patel did so in v2 [2, 3, 11, 12, 15]. Andrew Jones suggested placing Zi extensions before Zb extensions and asked for test configs, which were added in v2 [5, 10, 14, 19]. Conor Dooley questioned whether the XVentanaCondOps patches met the patch acceptance criteria for unratified vendor extensions, and Charlie Jenkins and Anup Patel debated how vendor extensions should be named and detected [21, 22, 24, 26]. Palmer Dabbelt's objection that the Veyron V1 was not publicly available led Anup Patel to drop the XVentanaCondOps patches, leaving the Zicond work [27, 29, 30, 33]. In v3 the series was reduced to six patches covering only Zicond and the selftests, and it was queued for Linux 6.7 after Palmer Dabbelt acked the Zicond detection patch with a request for a shared tag, which Anup Patel created [33, 34, 35, 36, 38].

commit.subject: RISC-V: Init and Halt Code

ai.summary: The RISC-V Linux port was submitted as a single series across three versions (v1 2017-06-28 was not the first, but v1 2017-05-23 through v8 2017-09-12, all by Palmer Dabbelt) and was structured as one large patch set that reviewers repeatedly asked to be split up for bisectability and for review [1, 70, 71, 72]. Early review focused on Makefile and Kconfig structure, requesting _defconfig naming, removal of redundant gitignore and Kconfig entries, and relocating drivers from arch/ to drivers/tty, drivers/irqchip and drivers/clocksource [3, 15, 19, 22, 25]. Reviewers also raised concerns about the memory model, MMIO barriers, mmiowb semantics and the atomic implementation, which were addressed by rewriting the I/O accessors and atomics with explicit fences and acquire/release variants, while the formal memory model was still pending a RISC-V working group specification [24, 29, 45, 52, 79, 85, 126, 127]. Concerns about the atomics syscall and 64-bit CAS on 32-bit systems, the PLIC's MMIO layout and interrupt-controller device-tree bindings, and sparse and checkpatch cleanliness were raised and largely resolved through follow-up changes [12, 26, 50, 60, 76, 77, 111, 143, 154, 165, 172]. Across versions the series was progressively split into separate patch sets for drivers and PCI support, the Kconfig and uapi build infrastructure was reworked, and the atomics and syscall interface were rewritten, with some items (such as the Kbuild uapi split and the bindings resubmission) still open at v8 [123, 124, 125, 173, 174, 178].

commit.subject: RISC-V: Add Zicboz detection and block size parsing

7ea5a73617e9.title: RISC-V: Apply Zicboz to clear_page and memset

ai.summary: The series, by Andrew Jones, adds Zicboz support so that clear_page() can zero memory using cbo.zero on naturally aligned block-sized chunks, with a dynamic instruction count reported as just over a quarter of the old count [1, 9, 23, 39, 50]. An earlier v1 also tried to apply Zicboz to memset(), but the memset() patches were dropped in v2 because it was unclear whether that would be a win, and only clear_page() remained [9, 15, 16, 17, 18, 50]. The main points raised were the DT binding for a separate cboz-block-size property, with reviewers settling on requiring it explicitly rather than falling back to cbom-block-size [10, 11, 13, 14, 16, 20]. Another point was how to patch in the Zicboz alternative: the vendor_id approach was replaced by using the upper 16 bits of the patch ID, after Conor Dooley noted that vendor_id was unsafe to repurpose [25, 26, 31, 32, 40, 41]. Reviewers also asked for the block-size check to guard against overflow with a memset fallback, and for the clear_page symbol to be exported correctly for modules [21, 22, 33, 42, 47, 48]. Across versions the series grew from a v1 covering memset() and clear_page() to a v2 focused solely on clear_page(), with v3 adding the DT documentation and v4 through v6 reworking the alternatives mechanism, the fallback, and the export, before it was accepted for for-next with KVM exposure acked by Anup Patel [36, 44, 45, 50, 51, 53].

commit.subject: riscv: Add support for Zicbop

earlier.title: riscv: Use Zicbop in arch_xchg when available
riscv: Introduce Zicbop instructions
riscv: Add ARCH_HAS_PREFETCH[W] support with Zicbop

ai.summary: The Zicbop series adds support for the Zicbop prefetch extension and then uses it to enable the kernel's prefetch features, with Guo Ren's earlier work revived and respun by Alexandre Ghiti as v3 [1]. The threads show that the v3 changelog records fixes made in response to reviewer comments from Drew, including a typo fix, splitting the first patch, and adding prefetch support [1]. Guo's comments on v3 led to moving PREFETCHW_ASM out of an ifdef, and the prefetch instructions were changed so that bits [0:4] are zeroed and the CBO_ prefix was dropped [1]. Compared with v2, the series was separated from the qspinlock work, the coding convention was adjusted, DEFINE_INSN_S was added to insn-def.h, and CBO_PREFETCH_I/R/W were introduced [1]. Andrea Parri gave a Tested-by tag for the v3 series [2].

commit.subject: arch/riscv: add Zihintpause support

ai.summary: The Zihintpause series adds support for the PAUSE hint in the RISC-V cpu_relax() path across four versions from Dao Lu, from May to June 2022 [1, 2, 6, 7]. Samuel Holland first argued that, because PAUSE is a hint and harmless if unsupported, no runtime probe was needed [3], but Atish Patra noted that without a probe older platforms would execute a nop instead of the div that previously provided the stall [4, 5]. Palmer Dabbelt then favoured runtime probing via the alternatives mechanism so that pre-Zihintpause hardware kept its existing behaviour [6]. Heiko Stuebner asked for a rebase onto the unified static key mechanism and for a commit message with more background [1, 7], and Samuel Holland and Dao Lu discussed moving to that mechanism in v3 [9, 10]. The series was merged for-next in v4 after reviews from Guo Ren, Atish Patra, and Heiko Stuebner [11, 12, 16], and was later reported to break some builds with newer binutils and with sparse C=1 checks [17, 19, 20]. Andrew Jones responded with a fix, and Samuel Holland raised further build failures with CONFIG_CC_OPTIMIZE_FOR_SIZE and a suggestion to run both instructions unconditionally instead of using a static branch in cpu_relax() [21, 22].

commit.subject: RISC-V: Detect AIA CSRs from ISA string

8fe6f7e14c7e.title: RISC-V: Detect AIA CSRs from ISA string

ai.summary: The series adds Linux irqchip drivers for the RISC-V AIA specification, covering the AIA CSRs, the IMSIC per-HART MSI controller and the APLIC wired interrupt controller, along with DT bindings and a MAINTAINERS entry [1, 40]. Early reviews raised a lock-context problem in the IMSIC driver, where `priv->ids_lock` was taken from hardirq context without irqsave handling [4, 32], a boot hang seen with 8 CPUs [2, 3], and a warning splat from zeroed MSI messages in the APLIC driver during free_irq [5, 6]. Device-tree binding review focused on compatible strings, with reviewers objecting to a placeholder vendor string and to the plural "imsics" name, and the author settled on a QEMU-specific compatible string [8, 10, 26, 31]; reviewers also asked for clearer descriptions of the `riscv,children`, `riscv,delegate` and `msi-parent`/`interrupts-extended` properties, which the author explained in responses that were then reflected in the revised text [9, 35, 36, 59, 61, 62]. Between v1 and v2 the author rebased onto Linux 6.2-rc2, switched to `raw_spin_lock_irqsave()`, fixed the APLIC MSI write warning, dropped the `riscv,slow-ipi` property, and revised the bindings [40]. The later v3 and v4 revisions are a separate series that virtualizes the AIA CSRs in KVM RISC-V, where v3 was reworked into smaller patches and v4 split the per-HART CSR patch further and addressed review comments, with the author noting the final patch depends on the RISC-V IPI series [63, 84, 93]. Among the v1 AIA driver review, Marc Zyngier's v2 comments asked for splitting, removal of unused KVM-only exports, and a real IPI in place of sideband signalling, which the author agreed to address in part [48, 94, 95].

commit.subject: RISC-V: Add Svade and Svadu Extensions Support

94a7734d0967.title: Add Svade and Svadu Extensions Support

earlier.title: Add Svadu Extension Support

ai.summary: The Svade and Svadu series adds support for the two PTE accessed/dirty (A/D) management schemes, Svade (software-managed, page fault on update) and Svadu (hardware updating), for both host and guest kernels [1, 53]. Reviewers spent most of the v5 discussion on how the four device-tree combinations of svade and svadu should be interpreted, in particular the case where neither property is present, which was treated as technically unknown and left to supervisor software to handle either behaviour [2, 6, 10, 18, 25, 34, 36]. Concerns that old firmware could leave svadu in the device tree without enabling it were raised, with the view that platforms must describe their hardware correctly and that QEMU's default behaviour was consistent with the binding [22, 23, 26, 27, 30, 31]. The binding text was reworded several times, with reviewers asking that it state the requirements explicitly ("must" and "may"), drop the speculative mvendorid/marchid/mimpid discovery and "(Obvious)" remarks, and refer to the ratified Svadu manual rather than the archived repository [5, 7, 34, 39, 43, 47, 49, 52]. Clément Léger's suggestion to use the extension .validate callbacks replaced the earlier duplicated code in the cpufeature changes [48, 51], and a reviewer's request to keep the Svade check in the KVM henvcfg condition was restored in v8 [44, 46]. Across versions the series moved from v5's initial enablement to v6 and v7 changes that reflected platform behaviour through riscv_isa_extension_available() and refined the binding, then to v8, which added a compile-error fix to the get-reg-list selftest as a separate patch [33, 38, 53, 54]. The series was queued for Linux 6.13 after the selftest fix went through the KVM RISC-V tree [55, 56, 57, 58, 59].

commit.subject: RISC-V: Detect Smstateen extension

earlier.title: KVM: riscv: selftests: Add smstateen registers to get-reg-list test

ai.summary: The series adds detection of the Smstateen extension for the host and for guest VCPUs, and exposes senvcfg and sstateen0 through the KVM ONE_REG interface with matching context save/restore [1, 9, 11]. Conor Dooley asked that the motivation and the reason only KVM needs the support be stated in the series, and that the motivation appear in the cover letter as well as the patch description [5, 7]. Anup Patel supplied the spec rationale: covert channels between user threads or guest OSes via extension state the hypervisor does not context-switch, so hstateen0 must gate VS-mode access to AIA state and envcfg, with bit 0 of the stateen CSRs controlling access to custom registers that higher privilege levels should only enable when they know how to switch them [6, 8]. Dooley also questioned how bit 0 interacts with unknown custom extensions and noted that /proc/cpuinfo is a poor way to detect such support, a concern left unresolved in the thread [7]. Dooley gave a Reviewed-by on the device tree bindings patch, which was split out into its own patch in v3 [4]. Over the versions, the DT bindings change moved into a separate patch, the senvcfg and sstateen0 save/restore moved into their own functions, the commit description of the detection patch was expanded, and the series was rebased, with the final v5 rebased on latest master [2, 3, 9, 11]. Dooley also asked that the detection patch be shared with the riscv tree to avoid a merge conflict in that area [10]. Anup Patel queued the series for Linux 6.7 [12].

commit.subject: RISC-V: Add Smcntrpmf extension parsing

earlier.title: dt-bindings: riscv: add Smcntrpmf ISA extension description

ai.summary: The Smcntrpmf-related work sits inside a larger series, "Add Counter delegation ISA extension support" by Atish Patra, which adds support for the S[m|s]csrind indirect CSR extensions and the Smcdeleg/Ssccfg counter delegation extensions so that S-mode can program hpmevent and hpmcounter registers directly rather than through SBI calls [1, 8, 74, 90, 141]. Smcntrpmf is one of the extensions in this dependency set, and its binding and parsing patches were reviewed by Rob Herring's bot, Conor Dooley, Clément Léger and others [2, 3, 6, 13, 25, 31, 126, 127]. Early reviews flagged dt-binding YAML tab and indentation errors, a missing frozen-spec reference, misordered extension listings, and a dependency that belonged in the schema rather than in prose [2, 5, 9, 13, 16, 17, 20]. Reviewers also asked for validation callbacks encoding inter-extension dependencies, and the author responded by noting that Smcntrpmf is strictly required by Smcdeleg/Ssccfg only for some registers, so only always-required extensions were validated [23, 24, 32, 63]. The series was reshaped across versions from v1 through v9: the RFC was reworked after perf-tool and event-encoding discussions, the driver file/function renames were reverted at Will Deacon's request, the counter discovery and event mapping mechanisms were reworked, and Paul Walmsley queued the early prerequisite patches to riscv for-next while the remainder moved toward the v7.4 window [1, 8, 12, 19, 21, 29, 34, 43, 74, 90, 119, 130, 141, 152].

commit.subject: riscv: Add ISA extension parsing for Svvptc

a6efe33cc594.title: Svvptc extension to remove preventive sfence.vma

ai.summary: The series, first posted as an RFC and now at v4, adds Svvptc probing and a devicetree binding, then removes the preventive sfence.vma after new vmalloc mappings (handled by trap in the early exception path) and after new user mappings, relying on gratuitous page faults instead [1, 15, 22]. Reviewers asked for the correct To/Cc list and tested-by workflow [2], questioned why the xRET property was needed and asked for the perf numbers to be folded into the cover letter [3], and Alexandre reported that the Svvptc spec author had dropped the xRET fence behaviour, so userspace mappings now take some extra page faults [4, 5]. Discussion of the vmalloc entry path covered whether to use percpu variables versus thread_info, with the objection that kernel stacks live in vmalloc space ruling out the stack, and a suggestion to make the fence removal a Kconfig option that was rejected in favour of alternatives [7, 8, 9, 10, 11, 12, 13, 14]. In v3 the RFC tag was dropped after ratification, the xRET-as-fence comment was removed, and sfence.vma counts were added to the cover letter [15, 3]; v4 fixed rv32 and amoswap width issues, saved only the needed registers, and fixed an LLVM build error [17, 18, 19, 16, 22]. A 2026 report (not addressed in any v4 reply) argues that a stale invalid translation cached before the vmalloc PTE is installed can coexist with a later valid entry, so the short return-to-user window after sscratch is restored may skip new_vmalloc_check, and asks whether the scheme assumes this cannot happen [24].

commit.subject: RISC-V: add zbb support to string functions

b6fcdb191e36.title: Zbb string optimizations and call support in alternatives

earlier.title: HACK: RISC-V: add zbb support to string functions
arch/riscv : Add support for Zba/Zbb/Zbc/Zbs ext in ISA realization
Zbb + fast-unaligned string optimization

ai.summary: The series adds Zbb-optimised string functions (strcmp, strlen, strncmp) that are selected at runtime via alternatives, which required reviewers to address how alternatives handle auipc/jalr call addresses and instruction-level fixups [1, 16, 17, 26, 31]. Early discussion questioned whether libstub should be exempted from the optimised variants, and it was settled that it must be because the Zbb variants would otherwise produce build errors through unresolved references [2, 4, 5]. Reviewers raised repeated questions about the instruction-parsing header (naming, funct values, and consolidation of macros) and about extension ordering in cpu.c, which was resolved by moving Zbb into the correct place after Conor's reordering series [9, 10, 34, 36, 37, 38, 40, 41, 120, 142]. Ard Biesheuvel and Andrew Jones objected to the inline-wrapper approach and the stub-specific guards, and the series was reworked to use a generic function with an alternative jump into the optimised code [91, 92, 93, 95, 103, 104, 112, 113]. Between v1 and v5 the series grew from seven patches to two, with the cleanup and instruction-parsing work split out and the auipc/jal fixups handled in dependent series, while register-naming, label, and loop-alignment comments were applied across v4 and v5 [45, 80, 108, 145, 122, 124, 149, 150]. The final v5 was applied to Palmer's tree [150], and a later report of a missing root filesystem was bisected to the Zbb string commit [152].

commit.subject: riscv: Add Zawrs support for spinlocks

earlier.title: riscv: Add Zawrs support for spinlocks

ai.summary: The Zawrs series adds support for the wrs.nto and wrs.sto wait instructions, and across v1 to v3 (Andrew Jones, with Christoph Müllner's spinlock patch) it moved from wrs.sto to wrs.nto for kernel wait loops, added hwprobe export, and taught KVM to let guests use wrs.nto [1, 3, 20]. The main concern raised was that wrs.nto may never terminate when not configured to raise an exception, which could stall a hart, and that the Zawrs DT binding should not rely on Linux-specific assumptions [4, 5, 8, 9]. Conor Dooley argued that firmware should describe what it guarantees rather than the binding assuming more, and Charlie Jenkins pointed out that the spec's bounded-time wording could be read as allowing no time limit [4, 12]. Andrew Jones answered that the wait loop cannot rely on a store occurring or a specific interrupt arriving, and that the spec should be read as requiring termination; he then asked the RVI ARC to examine the issue, which reported that it did not see a need for concern [9, 19, 22]. Conor's acknowledgement of the DT binding in v3 settled that part [21], and the binding text was moved from the DT description to a code comment in v3 [20]. Palmer Dabbelt later merged the series after Anup Patel acked the KVM patches [28, 29, 30, 31], and a documentation note on the assumption that mstatus.TW is clear was deferred to boot.rst [24, 25, 26].

commit.subject: RISC-V: Add Zba, Zbs extension probing

c6699baf1064.title: RISC-V: Export Zba, Zbb to usermode via hwprobe

earlier.title: arch/riscv : Add support for Zba/Zbb/Zbc/Zbs ext in ISA realization

ai.summary: The series, which was applied to the kernel tree on 2023-06-19 after two revisions, detects the Zba, Zbb, and (in v2) Zbs extensions and exports them per hart to userspace through hwprobe so that glibc can use them when building hwcaps-based library search paths [1, 10, 16]. The first patch adds probing for Zba, and reviewers asked that Zbs be handled in the same way, which Evan Green took up in v2 [1, 10, 11, 13]. The second patch starts tracking ISA extensions per hart alongside the existing AND-ed mask, and Conor Dooley's request for a blank line before an if statement was incorporated [3, 10]. Conor also flagged a copy-paste error that used IMA_ZBB where EXT_ZBB was meant, and Evan fixed it in v2 [4, 9, 10]. Reviewers asked that the Zba and Zbs trailers from v1 be kept, and Evan restored them in v2 [11, 13]. Palmer Dabbelt noted that b4 ignored a Reviewed-by trailer from Heiko Stübner because of a From address mismatch, and Palmer added it manually, while Palmer also observed that Zbc was not included in the series [15, 17, 18].

commit.subject: riscv: Add ISA extension parsing for Zalasr

c9651fbc6051.title: riscv: Add Zalasr ISA exntesion support

ai.summary: The Zalasr series adds support for the RISC-V Zalasr extension, which provides real load-acquire and store-release instructions, and it went through RFC v1, v1, v2, v3 and v4 [1, 5, 7, 16, 26]. Reviewers raised a few concerns: Conor Dooley asked about the RFC tag and CC list and noted that the dt-bindings entries were out of order, which was fixed in v2 [2, 6, 7, 9]. Andrea Parri identified that mixing .aq/.rl annotations with fences broke the UNLOCK+LOCK ordering property, and proposed options that Xu Lu chose to pursue by applying acquire/release semantics to xchg/cmpxchg and then atomic operations [8, 10, 14, 16, 22, 23]. Guo Ren weighed the fence-based alternatives and the performance trade-offs of ld.aq versus a fence, and reviewed the instruction patch [11, 12, 13, 24, 25, 28]. Andrea also pointed out that LR/SC without Zacas or Zabha still lacks the required write-to-read ordering, that v3 changed fence semantics for non-Zalasr systems without that being noted in the changelog, and that the lowering should only change under zalasr, with smp_cond_load_acquire() worth considering [17, 19, 31]. Xu Lu's replies explained the reasoning for the fence changes and promised a separate commit with fuller changelog text, and v4 added atomic-operation changes and removed the arch-specific acquire/release fences [18, 19, 20, 26]. Paul Walmsley applied only the first four patches, leaving patches 5 to 8 pending Xu Lu's revisions based on Andrea's feedback, and Xu Lu confirmed the work would continue [32, 33].

commit.subject: riscv: zicfiss / zicfilp enumeration

earlier.title: riscv: zicfiss/zicfilp extension csr and bit definitions
riscv: zicfilp / zicfiss in dt-bindings (extensions.yaml)
riscv: dynamic (zicfiss) shadow call stack support
RISC-V: KVM: Add Zicfiss/Zicfilp support

ai.summary: The series adds user-mode control-flow integrity to RISC-V using the Zicfilp landing-pad and Zicfiss shadow-stack extensions, with arch-agnostic prctls, a map_shadow_stack syscall, and signal-handling support [1, 34, 145, 229, 309, 336]. Early reviewers asked that envcfg be saved and restored only on task switch and that the entry/exit path stay short [2, 3, 8], and they pushed for a 64-bit-only design and consistent VM_SHADOW_STACK handling across architectures [4, 5, 6, 27, 45]. Signal-context layout was reworked to avoid breaking pre-CFI binaries, which led to a vector-style context header [18, 95, 96, 106, 109], while the dt-bindings change was held until spec status and commit references were settled [51, 53, 59, 61, 64]. Later discussion covered a command-line switch (riscv_nousercfi), the two vDSO variants selected by hardware support, and an LTP mmap04 regression from the PROT_WRITE-to-VM_READ|VM_WRITE change in patch 06, which Gupta attributed to RISC-V reusing VM_WRITE for the shadow-stack encoding and for which a fix was promised but not yet posted as of the last message [310, 331, 332, 351, 352, 355, 356, 359, 360, 361]. Across versions the series went from v23 to v26 through mostly fix-up changes: checkpatch cleanups and a commit-description rewrite (v23 to v24), a riscv_nousercfi build fix (v25), an MMU dependency (v26), and a map_shadow_stack fix that returns the shadow-stack base address rather than the token location [309, 333, 336, 338, 347, 348].

commit.subject: riscv: add ISA extension parsing for bfloat16 ISA extension

e186c28dda11.title: riscv: add ISA extension parsing for bfloat16 ISA extension

ai.summary: The series adds parsing and hwprobe export for the bfloat16 extensions Zfbfmin, Zvfbfmin and Zvfbfwma, citing the ratified BF16 chapter of the riscv-isa-manual [1]. Clément Léger asked that the extensions also be exported in sys_hwprobe.c, which the author agreed to and added in v2 [2, 3, 4]. ai.summary: The series adds parsing and hwprobe export for a set of RISC-V ISA extensions, Zihintntl among them, so userspace can query them via the hwprobe syscall [1, 67]. Reviewers raised the question of how to handle bundled "shorthand" extensions such as Zvkn and Zvks, with options discussed for keeping them, unfolding them, or unfolding without keeping the shorthand [6], and Conor Dooley and Evan Green later agreed on a bundle mechanism where pure bundles like Zk only enable their sub-extensions while superset extensions like Zvbb keep their own ID [14, 52, 54]. Jerry Shih pointed out that Zvknha and Zvknhb are exclusive rather than a superset relationship, so they were not bundled together [45, 61, 64], and Clément Léger agreed to drop that treatment in V4 [65, 67]. Reviewers also asked for a comment on the safety of the ISA-check macro for bundled extensions [59], asked that the Zkr binding document the privilege level at which the seed CSR is accessible [56], and asked that the Zfa binding not reference hwprobe, which Léger removed [57, 66]. Between versions, the series was reworked from a 13-patch set into 18–20 patches, with the bundle mechanism added, Zbc and the scalar crypto extensions split out, and the Zfh and Zvfh patches and bindings reviewed and acked by Dooley and Green [3, 17, 55, 67].

ai.summary: The series adds RVA23U64 base-behavior detection so userspace can test conformance in one call, exposing the result via /proc/cpuinfo and hwprobe, and it was built up from Andrew Jones's RFC v1 [1, 13] through v2 to v5 by Guodong Xu [24, 36, 55, 67]. Along the way it adds parsing and hwprobe export for Zicclsm, Ziccamoa/Ziccif/Ziccrse/Za64rs, B, and Zic64b, plus a Zic64b dt-binding and device-tree declarations [4, 5, 7, 10, 11, 27, 41, 48, 63, 67]. Reviewers debated whether bundles like B should be exported through hwcap and hwprobe, and the community agreed to export B as a superset with a comment explaining why it is not a bundle [3, 8, 14, 18, 22, 23]. Reviewers also argued over whether RVA23U64 detection should depend on hwprobe bits or on ISA-string bits, with the consensus that it uses the ISA bitmap and that hwprobe export follows user need [6, 7, 11, 12, 16, 17, 19, 20, 28, 43]. Discussion of the Zic64b cache-block-size checks led to validating only the CBO block sizes that are present, a change credited to Qingwei Hu [38, 49, 50, 52, 54, 63], and Conor Dooley's objections to kernel-side validation callbacks led to the removal of the Ziccamoa and Za64rs dependency checks [60, 67]. Several dt-binding and sorting fixes were made in response to review, including sorting multi-letter Z extensions and requiring cbom/cbop/cboz block-size properties when the matching extension is present [30, 31, 37, 59, 62, 69, 74, 75, 76]. The series was reworked across versions from RFC v1 to v5, shrinking the scope of hwprobe exports and tightening dt-binding and validation logic, and patches were queued for v7.2 and v7.3 by Paul Walmsley [76, 77, 78, 79, 80, 81].

ai.summary: The Svpbmt series went through many revisions, with reviewers first debating where the feature should be described in devicetree: Anup Patel and Nick Kossifidis argued against changing the existing "mmu-type" property for compatibility and for per-CPU handling of heterogeneous cores, while Philipp Tomsich and others proposed a nested "mmu" node with boolean entries, and later reviewers including Jessica Clarke and Heiko Stuebner debated how that would interact with the ISA string and user-visible reporting [1, 3, 6, 7, 9, 32, 34, 35, 54, 59, 63, 66, 70, 73, 74, 76, 79]. A separate, contentious thread concerned Allwinner D1 PTE bits that conflict with the Svpbmt bit positions; reviewers including Atish Patra, Nick Kossifidis, Anup Patel, Philipp Tomsich and Palmer Dabbelt debated whether to accept such non-compliant hardware upstream and, if so, whether it should be gated behind a Kconfig option or runtime code patching, with the outcome that Svpbmt support would be kept runtime-patchable and that D1 memory types were added later via the alternatives framework [15, 16, 19, 20, 21, 24, 25, 26, 28, 83, 84]. Christoph Hellwig's review of v3 led to macros being replaced with clearer definitions, a Kconfig option being added, and naming and helper changes [36, 44, 45, 49, 95, 96]. Across versions, the series moved from a v1 modifying "mmu-type" in 2021, through v3 and v4 revisions adding a Kconfig symbol and a nested mmu/riscv,svpbmt boolean, to a 2022 v10 series that rewrote the feature around the alternatives framework with a separate early-patching stage, which was merged [33, 51, 71, 84, 85].
